column8: Mon 16 Nov: the statute's 'guaranteed annuity' form is the shape twin; row 2 carries the same law with its sharper point (fixed in amount, not paid); store Q55-042 quotes the same regulation.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a beside aha 5, the strongest legal reading of 'guaranteed' (determinable, not paid); fix the conceit clause: by CONCEIT's definition a CLAT annuity is pencil however firmly the deed writes it, so never 'ink in the deed', which uses ink as signed (card Q42).

Mon 16 Nov: store; the income-then-principal queue shows a shortfall reaches the charity last; keep 'own Treasury plus the extra Treasuries' and never 'no payment depends on another bond' (NUMBERS 2).

Mon 16 Nov: 3a aha 5, the 7520 rate is 120% of the 3-9 year mid-term rate by statute; 'a rate Treasuries cannot earn' overclaims in general (a steep curve can pay more at the long end): say it sits above the mid-term yields by law and today above every point of the 6 Nov curve (6.2% against a 5.29% top).

Mon 16 Nov: re-derived: 13.716% payout, nine paid in full, 34% of the tenth, 93.4% of the promise at a flat 5.08%; say 'at November 2026 rates', not 'by construction', since a steep curve differs; store or a 3a note at most.

Mon 16 Nov: re-derived $269,852, $314,416 and $479,507 (flat annual rates, 6-15 years from 1 Jan 2027); $301,544 and $336,656 match NUMBERS 1 and 2; an aha 5 exhibit line or store, labelled valuations, never plan figures.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the 1989 peak rests on two practitioner sources, IRS table only from 1997; supports 'a promise sized at one rate is a forecast in disguise'.
Mon 16 Nov: store; NUMBERS 1 figures ($297,636, $302,163, $301,544) match; a minor contrast for 2.5 (the market sets the price on the trade day).

Mon 16 Nov: 3a aha 5, a zeroed-out ladder is design A's twin; fix: the $1,414 spare is before the waiting fund's fee ($0 with it, NUMBERS 2), say 55.6% as one rate cycle (17.1% of starts 1962-80, 80.1% from 1981) with 585 starting months, and never as the submitted ten falling short.
Mon 16 Nov: store; a CLAT form of sequence risk (H3-033, H4-127 give the general idea); illustration on reordered S&P years via Lee et al. citing AllianceBernstein.

Mon 16 Nov: checked at source (slides 11-12): $1,358,677, -37% in 2008, $618,830 end-2013, 2014 payment $703,547, dry in year 9, $267,854 on the average path all hold; but the slide's 6.31% 'average annual return' is not the listed returns' average (10.0% arithmetic, about 8.0% compound 2006-14, Keel arithmetic): say the returns beat the 6% rate on average, not 6.31%; 14.8% unpaid holds.

Mon 16 Nov: checked at source: $100,000,023.56, $108,570,025.58 due, $94,104,550.57 paid, the $14,465,475.01 shortfall quote, $27.6875 to $26.1875: 86.7% paid, 13.3% short after a 5.4% fall hold; a GRAT, not a CLAT; store.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3a, one clause: when a lead trust runs dry the charity, not the donor, takes the loss; the residency carries no such risk for the ten (one firm's FAQ plus the ACTEC article).
Mon 16 Nov: store; a cautionary contrast for the strong true word: practitioners say 'regardless' of money no Treasury pays, while Laura's 'guaranteed' is true (Books 3, 5, 19).

Mon 16 Nov: 3a beside aha 5: US law tests a donor's annuity trust for running dry (5%) but not a charity's lead trust; say the stricter test is applied to the residency's ten payments, not 'the charity's money' (the residency's legal form is outside the case).
Mon 16 Nov: 3a store support for aha 5: the only exhaustion rule assumes the trust earns the 7520 rate, so it cannot see a rate fall; the CRAT form is H3-067.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a vivid contrast: the regulation deems one company's non-dividend stock sufficient 'even indefinitely' at an assumed rate; Laura's sufficiency is tested with no interest.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c legal precedent for counting only what is evident; use only beside aha 4, the one home of 'she states only what she owns'; the bottom's rule also charges the fund fee from the trade day (NUMBERS 0).
Mon 16 Nov: store; the 60% jeopardy condition is a tax condition, not a funding test.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3e line: the law judges the manager's care, not hindsight, so no rule requires a CLAT to pay; Laura's standard is a test of the money, not of the manager.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a store: the law's wall between charity money and private money mirrors her flexibility as a separate pot; for Laura it is her rule, never a legal bar (Q62 row 40).
Mon 16 Nov: store; a disanalogy in Laura's favour: CLATs take no top-ups, the IPS completes the ten in 2028; $2,388 and $35,894 match NUMBERS 2; H3-065 has the remainder-trust form.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a store: settling at the undiscounted face is the zero-interest measure; Rev. Rul. 88-27 read only in a secondary summary (S 2): drop that clause or read the ruling; a PLR binds only its taxpayer.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 2.0: checked at source (slide 22: $9,529,596, $1,083,229, $10,832,292, $7,170,581, $2,887,622, $4,282,959, DERISK); fix 'locked in January 2027': most of each payment is owned in January 2027, the rest and the extra Treasuries in January 2028.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 or 3b, the governing thought in a practitioner's words (duration-matched bonds for the charity, growth for the rest); fix: the 21.6% depleted is the 100% S&P CLAT on slide 15, not one that funds three years in cash, so never 'a careful CLAT gambles in 1 path in 5'.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b store; rewrite the mapping: in the CLAT more bonds raise the family's chance of anything left and cut its median; in Laura's plan more moved into Treasuries raises the stated top and costs about $5,300 of what she keeps per $5,000 (8o); 'buys certainty' is wrong.
Mon 16 Nov: the same split in a second practitioner's words; 'just enough at the 7520 rate' is Keel's reading of the quote.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3a contrast: lead trusts held 2.9% government bonds in 2012 (4.5% in 2006, Keel arithmetic re-derived), Laura's ten are all Treasuries; includes unitrusts and state bonds.
Mon 16 Nov: store; correlation only, and remainder-trust donors hold bonds for income, which weakens the parallel.
Mon 16 Nov: store; NUMBERS 1's 2042 rung ($23,168 for $29,021 face) matches; a loose analogy to back-loaded CLATs.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3.0, one sentence on the order of claims: a charitable annuity funded from what is left was left with nothing; Laura funds the ten first; emptied by estate tax, not markets; will read in a transcription.
Mon 16 Nov: store; reprints only and the January 2003 rate conflicts (3.6% against the IRS table's 4.2%).
Mon 16 Nov: the policy form of the same lesson (a rule sized at one rate met another rate world); the pre-1989 10% is unverified.
Mon 16 Nov: store; underwater GRATs in January 2009, GRATs not CLATs, no count of failed CLATs.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a and 3e reservoir; the one honest line is the weaker guard (no deed binds her, Q62 row 40); say '120% of the federal mid-term rate', and never call the plan a trust.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a, a sharper twin for aha 5's IRS clause (H3-066, H3-067); fix: '120% of the federal mid-term rate', 'paid even if cash waiting earns nothing' for 'sized with no interest', and drop 'the Treasuries that rate is built from' (3-9 year yields; her holdings run to 2041).
